title: Softlaunch signal curation sprint: checklist, calendar, and release-notes draft
content:
Purpose
This doc captures the lightweight playbook for the Softlaunch Signal Curation sprint: the small batch rollout we plan to run for Canary-2 (low-latency routing change + KV cache warmup). The aim is to validate signal quality, ensure no regression in tail latency, and gather annotated telemetry for Optimize rules. This is NOT the full launch runbook — it is intentionally narrow and conservative.

Audience
- Release Engineers (owners of the cutover window)
- Serving Runtime (on-call + owners)
- Observability / Metrics (SRE/Console)
- Product PM and Solutions Eng (customer impact watchers)

High-level rollout objective
- Move 0.5% -> 5% traffic to the new routing policy variant over 36 hours with automatic rollback on key gates.
- Validate: 99.9th latency change <= +15ms, token-error-rate delta <= 0.02%, and no increase in user-facing 5xx.
- Produce annotated traces for three customer classes (PLG sandbox, mid-market, enterprise) for Optimize to analyze batching and KV cache benefits.

Quick checklist (day-of)
- Preflight (T-48h):
  - Confirm terraform plan applied for canary pool: infra PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789) [owner: Priya].
  - Canary capacity reservation: Dedicated pool reservation created and annotated [owner: Ethan].
  - Observability hooks in place: synthetic runners for each signal class (PLG/mid/enterprise) with alert rules. Verify dashboards show green [owner: Sofia].
  - Release notes draft posted in #release-prep channel and pinned [owner: Ava].

- Preflight (T-3h):
  - Run smoke script (smoke/canary-2.sh) — passes for base model against 5 sample prompts (attach logs) [owner: Jordan].
  - KV cache warmup dry-run on staging using production prefix traces (sanitized) [owner: Serving Runtime].
  - Feature flags: ensure feature gate set to rampable with manual override (FF:route_new_kv_variant) [owner: Release Eng].

- Cutover window (T0 -> T+36h):
  - T0: Switch 0.5% traffic. Monitor immediate errors for 30m. [owner: on-call release eng].
  - T+3h: If no gate violations, increase to 2%. Run quick A/B quality eval on sampling set.
  - T+12h: Increase to 5% if healthy. Collect traces for 2h.
  - T+24h: Run full metrics comparison and signal-run notes collection.
  - T+36h: Decision checkpoint: promote to wider ramp or rollback.

Gates and rollback triggers (automated)
- Immediate rollback if: 5xx rate increases by >= 0.05% relative to baseline in 15m window.
- Conservative rollback if: 99.9th latency increases by > 30ms sustained for 30m.
- Quality gate: token-error-rate delta > 0.05% on sampled prompts -> pause and manual review.
- Observability gap trigger: if synthetic runner fails to report for >10m, pause ramp and investigate.

Checklists for key collaborators (annotated responsibilities)
- Observability / SRE (Sofia):
  - Ensure dashboards preloaded: canary-latency, token-errors, 5xx-by-route, prefix-cache-hit
  - Synthetic runners status: green 24h pre-cutover
  - Tracing: set sampling to capture 1 in 50 requests for canary lanes

- Serving Runtime (Ethan + Jordan):
  - Confirm kernel selection policy matches the model variant (quantization profile X)
  - Smoke test KV eviction boundary under tiny-burst scenario
  - Validate fallback mapping: when model variant unavailable traffic routes to fallback v1

- Release Engineers (Ava + Priya):
  - Update canary escalation list in this doc and #release-escalations
  - Keep Slack thread pinned and post status updates at each checkpoint
  - After action: collect annotated decision timeline and example traces for RG Optimize

Rollforward vs rollback decision template (for T+36h meeting)
- Observed metrics (copy/paste): baseline vs canary deltas (latency p50/p95/p99/p999, 5xx rate, token-error-rate)
- Qualitative notes: any customer-facing reports, support tickets, manual QA notes
- Action: promote to 25% ramp / hold / rollback to v1
- If promote: define next ramp cadence and owners for next 72h

Release notes draft (short form)
- Title: Canary-2: routing + KV warmup softlaunch (Apr 2026)
- Summary: Introduces a routing policy that prioritizes low-sequence requests to the optimized KV-warm variant, aiming to reduce per-token cost for short prompts while maintaining latency SLOs.
- Impact: Small percentage of traffic routed to new variant (configurable). No expected API changes. Customers using dedicated pools are unaffected unless opt-in.
- Known limitations: Early metrics may underrepresent benefits due to cold prefix cache; we will gather annotated traces and follow up with Optimize recommendations.
- Rollout plan: 0.5% -> 5% over 36 hours with automated rollback gates.
- Contacts: release@redwood.com, oncall-release, obs-sre@redwood.com

Field notes / loose thoughts (brainstorm fragments)
- Consider adding a short lived header (X-Canary-Trace) that the Optimize pipeline can use to bias analysis for this run. Quick-win for sample selection.
- Is there merit to running an additional traffic slice limited to enterprise customers for 6h (explicit consent)? Pros: higher-value traces. Cons: risk / contract implications. Tag for product decision.
- Telemetry: capture model selection reason in traces (why routing chose variant) — could be a fast follow in runtime PR.

Unresolved questions (TBD before T0)
- Do legal/enterprise contracts require pre-notice for any routing experiments on enterprise traffic? (action: Product ask)
- Are SLO dashboards configured to show delta vs week-prior baseline (not just immediate baseline)? Observability to answer.

Appendix: Quick command snippets
- smoke run: ./scripts/smoke_canary2.sh --endpoint canary2 --prompts examples/smoke-set.json > /tmp/smoke.log
- rollback: /infra/scripts/ff_toggle.sh route_new_kv_variant off --expedite --by=release-team
- collect traces: /obs/collect_traces --filter "canary2 or X-Canary-Trace" --since 2026-04-21T00:00Z --out traces/canary2-annotated.json

Post-mortem & after action deliverables (if promoted)
- 72h ramp report: annotated metrics and cost impact estimate (owner: Product + Engage)
- Telemetry artifacts: curated trace set for Optimize (owner: Observability + Applied ML)
- Public release note update: add performance numbers and recommendations for customers (owner: Docs)

Quick timeline snapshot
- 2026-04-18: Kickoff and infra PR merged
- 2026-04-20 09:00: Synthetic runners green
- 2026-04-21 10:00: Cutover T0 planned (this runbook)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the first 3 hours hyper-alert. Historically the interesting problems show up in map-step routing + cache inconsistency.
- If we see noise on p999 only, consider increasing sample size rather than immediate rollback unless 5xx spikes.

End of doc — add any live links to thread and attach logs here prior to T0.
